started:
Started {handle} without an opening. Link: {url}
Next: call add_slides now with only the opening, the title slide and one or two short spoken sentences. Its reply says when the link is playable.
project: Project folder: {root}. file= paths and rev= read from it; if that is the wrong folder, start again with project_dir set to the right absolute path.
no_project: No project folder, so file= and rev= cannot read code. Pass project_dir, an absolute path, to start_walkthrough.
playable:
Playable after {seconds} s: {url}
Send this link to the user now, in a message, before your next tool call. Then send the first content slide alone and short, so it is ready within seconds; after that, one to three whole slides per add_slides call. The authoring guide follows.
pending:
Slides saved. The opening audio is still being made, but the link already works: {url}
Share it with the user now; playback starts when the audio is ready. Then keep adding slides.
voice_error:
Slides saved, but voicing failed: {error}
Link: {url}. Continue with the next add_slides call. If the error repeats, stop and ask the user to run `showntell doctor`.
need_opening: Nothing to play yet: no narration so far. Send one or two spoken sentences next, as plain paragraphs without a heading; they join the last slide you sent. A > line is shown, not spoken.
finished:
Finished: {slides} slides, {duration}. {url}
Tell the user the walkthrough is finished and give them the link. Do not repeat the script.
finished_fix:
Finished: {slides} slides, {duration}. {url}
Not ready for the user yet: the findings below name slides {fix}. Fix each with revise_slide now; its reply re-checks the slide, and for a layout finding (text_too_small, overflow, drawing_overlap) preview_slides on that slide draws it again. No need to finish again. Once they are fixed, tell the user the walkthrough is finished and give them the link. Do not repeat the script.
loading: The voice model is not ready yet: {status}. Send the opening with add_slides anyway; that reply may take longer, and it gives the link either way.
guide_send_link: If the user lacks the link, send it now, then keep writing.
guide_tell_user: **Tell the user** it is finished, with the link, in a line or two; don't repeat the script.
exported:
Saved {path} ({mb} MB, {duration}).
Send this file to the user as an attachment, through the channel you talk to them on, with a line on what it covers. The path is not a link: give it as one only if the user works on this machine. Don't repeat the script.
export_shrunk: Shrunk to fit {limit} MB: {what}. If the user's channel takes larger files and quality matters, export again with a higher max_mb.
export_silent: {n} narration paragraph(s) failed to voice and are silent in this file. Revise those slides to voice them again, then export again before sending.
alike: Slides {ids} in a row look alike ({look}); pictures of them follow when they could be drawn. Before you tell the user, give one of them a different look with revise_slide: takeaways beside the visual with `.side`, a second visual with `.pair`, `.full`, or another kind of visual. Keep a run only if it is one sequence the viewer should read as such.
no_walkthrough: No walkthrough {wid}. list_walkthroughs lists yours; the id is the part of the handle before the dot.
